notes:
Lead: Foxglove builds compact AI assistants for SMB support teams. Inbound trial via hosted API. Primary ask: streaming chat with tool-calls and strict JSON output for downstream orchestration. Current pain: when using JSON mode + function schema, responses sometimes arrive as text or truncated JSON fragments in stream, causing their parser to fail repeatedly. Dev quote: "We need guaranteed valid JSON for each function call result — retrying on parser errors is not an option for our pipeline."

Observations from logs: partial/fragmented JSON appears when response > ~1.2k tokens; some cases where model chose a free-text reply instead of invoking configured function (schema mismatch?). Customer used SDK v1.2.3 and their function schema includes nested objects; they reported differences between our example schemas and their generated 'parameters' block (required vs properties layout). They attempted a server-side assembly approach (buffering stream until EOF) but streaming is needed to hit latency SLOs.

They are cost-sensitive (SMB budget) but prioritize reliability for their orchestration layer. Security: SSO required later, currently ok with hosted API keys. SE has suggested two immediate paths: 1) show canonical minimal repro + config for JSON mode + streaming assembly patterns; 2) run a short PoC on hosted dedicated route with stricter model variant that favors function-calling determinism. Customer prefers option 1 first.

Notes style: fragments, paraphrases of CTO and eng lead, logs referenced. Wants a scheduled deep-dive and an actionable repro they can run in < 2 hours.
technical_requirements: Latency target: p95 < 300ms for short chat (<=512 tokens) and streaming with first-byte < 150ms; throughput modest (100 reqs/min). Must support function-calling with strict JSON output, stable schema validation (nested objects), and ability to fall back to textual errors with clear error codes. SDK integration on Node and Python. No on-prem at this stage.
